chunks: "Indeed, the number of the months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth."

So the foremost of the months is the Month of Allah, and it is the Month of Ramadan; and the heart of the Month of Ramadan is Laylat al-Qadr. And the Qur'an was sent down on the first night of the Month of Ramadan, so receive the month with the Qur'an."
The compiler of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The descent of the Qur'an was completed on Laylat al-Qadr.

key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: the divine revelation sent down in Ramadan
key_terms.شَهْرُ اللَّهِ: the month specially ascribed to Allah, referring here to Ramadan
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the blessed month of fasting and Qur'anic revelation
key_terms.عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ: the divinely appointed count of the months
key_terms.فَاسْتَقْبِلِ الشَّهْرَ بِالْقُرْآنِ: welcome the month by engaging with the Qur'an
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree, described here as the heart of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Why is the Month of Ramadan called the Month of Allah and what is the significance of Laylat al-Qadr in it?
ai.summary: This hadith connects the Qur'anic mention of the twelve months to the special rank of the Month of Ramadan, calling it the Month of Allah. It identifies Laylat al-Qadr as the heart of Ramadan and urges welcoming the month through recitation of the Qur'an, while the compiler notes that the Qur'an's descent was completed on Laylat al-Qadr.
